questions.q: Plan an investigation into how the concentration of acid affects the rate of reaction with magnesium ribbon. Portal response box.
questions.a: IV: acid concentration (range of 5) (1); DV: time to stop fizzing or gas volume in a gas syringe (1); controls: length of Mg, volume of acid, temperature (1); method steps (1); repeat and mean (1); safety: eye protection, acid irritant (1).
questions.model: Teacher writes the variables first, then the first step: 'Measure 25 cm³ of 0.5 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid into a conical flask using a measuring cylinder.'

questions.q: Explain why a gas syringe gives more accurate results than counting bubbles.
questions.a: Bubbles vary in size (1); gas syringe measures volume directly (1); smaller resolution, all gas collected (1).

questions.q: Explain the difference between repeatable and reproducible.
questions.a: Repeatable: same person, same method gets similar results (1); reproducible: different people or methods get similar results (1).

questions.q: Identify the IV, DV and two controls: 'How does light intensity affect the rate of photosynthesis in pondweed?'
questions.a: IV: light intensity (distance of lamp) (1); DV: bubbles of oxygen per minute (1); controls: temperature, CO₂ concentration, same pondweed (1).
questions.model: IV: the thing changed: light intensity (lamp distance). DV: the thing measured: oxygen bubbles per minute. Controls: anything else that affects rate: temperature, CO₂.
